title: Generic migration wave 1, remote blocker, and pipes frontier
goal: Diagnose the remote amd64 exec-agent blocker without claiming remote success, wire generic resource graph coverage into routine validation, prepare careful PR hygiene, and advance the next consolidation path by proving a generic resource graph migration wave 1 contract plus a separate pipes/stdio graduation contract.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the remote amd64 EXEC_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE/write EPIPE blocker is isolated to a concrete layer or recorded as a bounded infrastructure blocker, distinguishing VMM binary selection, gvproxy binary selection, guest agent startup, guest boot, remote host resource pressure, and matrix harness behavior, without claiming remote generic success unless a targeted remote generic proof actually passes.
proofChecklist.evidence: Remote amd64 exec-agent blocker diagnosed as a bounded infrastructure blocker at the guest exec-agent/vsock transport layer after successful VMM boot, not as VMM binary selection, gvproxy binary selection, short guest-agent startup delay, remote host resource exhaustion, or matrix harness behavior. Commands ran on root@192.168.0.8 in /mnt/shared-500G/machinen-move-proof with MACHINEN_VMM=$PWD/packages/native-x64-linux/vmm/bin/machinen-vm and MACHINEN_GVPROXY=$PWD/packages/native-x64-linux/vmm/bin/gvproxy. Retained artifacts: /tmp/generic-remote-exec-agent-diagnosis-1781213669 and /tmp/generic-remote-exec-agent-wait-diagnosis-1781213814 on the remote host. host-preflight.txt records both VMM and gvproxy as ELF x86-64, remote uname x86_64, available memory/disk, /dev/kvm and /dev/vhost-vsock existence, and normal host resource state. boot.rc=0 and list-after-boot.json showed a live VM pid 3894764, so guest boot/VMM launch succeeded. Narrow exec probes true, uname -m, cat /proc/cmdline, and printf exec-agent-ok all failed with EXEC_AGENT_UNAVAILABLE: VsockExec.run: agent did not respond within 30000ms: write EPIPE. A second wait diagnosis booted a VM and retried exec after waits 0, 5, 15, and 30 seconds; every attempt failed with the same error, ruling out a short startup delay. The same failure happens before matrix-specific generic code, so it is not a generic matrix semantic failure. diagnosis-summary.json records classification=bounded-infrastructure-blocker: guest exec-agent/vsock transport unavailable after successful VMM boot. No remote generic success is claimed.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove remote cleanup and artifact retention are safe after diagnosis: no leaked remote VMs remain, commands and logs are retained under a named remote artifact directory, and any failed probe has enough evidence for follow-up debugging.
proofChecklist.evidence: Remote cleanup and artifact retention verified. Diagnosis artifacts are retained under /tmp/generic-remote-exec-agent-diagnosis-1781213669 and /tmp/generic-remote-exec-agent-wait-diagnosis-1781213814 on root@192.168.0.8, including host-preflight.txt, boot/list/exec rc/out/err files, host-vsock-kvm.txt, and diagnosis-summary.json. stop commands were run for both diagnostic VMs. list-after-stop.json in both artifact dirs shows vms=[]. A stale gvproxy process from an earlier run was discovered in host-vsock-kvm.txt/processes-before-stale-cleanup.txt while list showed no VMs; it was killed, and final verification with node packages/cli/dist/cli.js list --json returned {vms:[]} and ps showed no machinen-vm/gvproxy processes except the grep command itself. The first stale-cleanup command had a remote shell quoting mistake and did not kill the process; this was recorded in currentEvidence and corrected with remote-side variable expansion.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove a durable generic resource graph migration wave 1 contract exists for converting 5-10 simple bespoke envelopes to generic-primary or generic-equivalent behavior while preserving bespoke fallback, exact refusal evidence, target evidence, and honest non-claims.
proofChecklist.evidence: Created durable migration contract .pi/goals/generic-resource-graph-migration-wave1.json with 8 proof rows covering candidate selection, genericResourceGraphState descriptor proof, generic-primary/load selection versus bespoke fallback, equivalent target evidence, exact fail-closed refusals, migration coverage tooling, docs/PR language, and final validation. The contract has valid JSON, status=IN_PROGRESS, and nextAction to inventory candidate bespoke envelopes against generic proof rows. It explicitly preserves app-specific/bespoke fallback and forbids migration that removes fallback priority before equivalent generic happy-path and refusal evidence exists.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove the migration wave 1 candidate list is grounded in existing evidence and explicitly decides python-http, python-http-directory, nc-listener, reader-cat, grep, and tail, with tail accepted only if offset semantics are preserved or honestly refused.
proofChecklist.evidence: Added docs/snapshot/generic-resource-graph-migration-wave1.md with explicit candidate decisions grounded in existing generic evidence. Decisions: python-http is generic-equivalent first using generic-static-http-daemon evidence and keeps bespoke fallback; python-http-directory is generic-equivalent first using cwd/data-dir plus HTTP evidence and keeps bespoke fallback; nc-listener is a generic-equivalent candidate using generic-interpreted-server idle loopback TCP evidence and keeps nc fallback for nc-specific argv/binary behavior; reader-cat is generic-equivalent for readonly regular-file identity using generic-file-backed-worker evidence and keeps fallback for offset/stdio-sensitive behavior; grep is generic-equivalent for readonly-file CLI output using generic-readonly-file-cli evidence and keeps fallback for pattern/offset/stdin/pipe shapes; tail is explicitly not generic-primary in wave 1 unless offset/follow semantics are preserved exactly, and otherwise remains bespoke fallback with generic refusal/defer boundary. The doc also lists required refusal boundaries and required target evidence before any candidate can become generic-primary.

proofChecklist.obligation: Prove a durable generic pipes/stdio graduation contract exists, covering stdio policy, pipe peer graph, producer/consumer lifecycle, no hidden shell state, partial/unknown pipe refusal, happy-path support evidence, refusal evidence, and target-native loader boundaries.
proofChecklist.evidence: Created durable pipes/stdio graduation contract .pi/goals/generic-pipes-stdio-graduation.json with 9 proof rows. The contract covers descriptor fields for stdio policy and pipe peer graph; capture/classification for /dev/null, closed stdio, inherited noninteractive stdio, anonymous pipes, named FIFOs, shell pipelines, missing peers, fan-in/fan-out, and PTY/terminal refusal; producer/consumer lifecycle rules for finite replay, long-running pairs, EOF/shutdown, partial writes, blocked reads/writes, and process exit ordering; no hidden shell state; target-native loader preflight/fd reconstruction/launch ordering; happy-path and refusal matrix rows; docs/coverage; and final validation. Stop conditions forbid arbitrary shell pipeline, PTY, terminal, or process teleportation claims and forbid accepting partial/unknown pipe state or nontrivial inherited stdio without proof.
